decisions.question: How should Atlas use the Starbucks design experiment while preparing for its final identity?
options: Keep screen-level trademark assets
Use Starbucks visual grammar with one replaceable BrandMark boundary
Retain the previous Atlas light-green system
decisions.decision: Use Starbucks visual grammar as Atlas's primary design authority and centralize the temporary test mark in one replaceable BrandMark component.
decisions.rationale: The Product Owner approved the visual-system migration, confirmed that the current mark is temporary, and required a one-change replacement boundary.

decisions.question: How should VS-14 handle the inherited five-tab navigation while the design baseline describes four primary destinations?
options: Restructure navigation in VS-14
Preserve the existing navigation model for the bounded visual migration and defer alignment
Silently redefine the baseline
decisions.decision: Preserve the existing navigation model for VS-14 and defer alignment to a separate governed navigation slice.
decisions.rationale: The Product Owner explicitly instructed Atlas to preserve the navigation model, and VS-14 must not become an architecture rewrite.

decisions.question: How should VS-15 handle the inherited five-tab navigation while the approved baseline describes four persistent destinations?
options: Restructure navigation in VS-15
Preserve the existing navigation model for the bounded Context visual migration and defer alignment
Silently redefine the baseline
decisions.decision: Preserve the existing navigation model for VS-15 and defer navigation alignment to a separate governed slice.
decisions.rationale: The Product Owner approved the planned bounded migration sequence and instructed that existing navigation be preserved; repeating the migration for Context must not become a navigation or architecture rewrite.

decisions.question: Which public sources should the first Category Intelligence discovery slice support?
options: Keep Wolt/Bolt public pages only
Support ordinary HTTPS business websites plus Wolt/Bolt through a provider-neutral safe public snapshot
Add private provider/POS connectors now
decisions.decision: Support ordinary HTTPS public business websites plus Wolt and Bolt Food public pages through a provider-neutral Public Business Snapshot, with conservative extraction, owner confirmation and SSRF-safe fetching. Private connectors remain out of scope.
decisions.rationale: The Product Owner explicitly approved the recommended VS-16 scope including normal public business websites plus Wolt/Bolt and instructed implementation to proceed through completion.

decisions.question: How should VS-17 collect optional category-aware onboarding context?
options: Generate onboarding questions dynamically with AI
Show a fixed static form per category
Use a deterministic versioned skippable catalogue selected from missing context
decisions.decision: Use a deterministic, versioned, server-owned and fully skippable progressive-question catalogue. Create the Business first, select only 3–5 highest-value missing questions, present them tap-first one at a time, persist answers as owner-confirmed Business Context, and persist skip/answer progress separately for resumability.
decisions.rationale: The Product Owner approved skippable questions, deterministic versioning, tap-first one-question-at-a-time interaction, post-Business sequencing, all eight initial category families plus Generic fallback, and suppression of skipped questions unless a future explicit material-value trigger justifies re-asking.

decisions.question: How should URL-first onboarding resolve operating location and dependent market metadata, including multi-location businesses?
options: Keep manual country/timezone/currency fields
Auto-select the first address found without owner review
Resolve a Business location, let the owner select among branches when ambiguous, use Google Places search when unknown, and derive country/timezone/currency automatically
decisions.decision: Treat the operating location as the owner-facing choice. Preselect one strong branch but keep it changeable; show branch cards when multiple matches exist; use Google Places Text Search (New) when location is unknown; obtain canonical address, coordinates, country and IANA timezone from the same Places response; derive ISO currency inside Atlas; onboard one location first and add other branches later. Do not call the separate Google Time Zone API in this slice.
decisions.rationale: The Product Owner explicitly required automatic country/timezone/currency selection and branch choice, then approved the recommended lower-cost refinement to use Places timeZone in the same Text Search response and remove the separate Time Zone API dependency.

decisions.question: How should Atlas retain restaurant images and menu data discovered from public business sources?
options: Copy and rehost third-party image binaries and raw menu pages
Store provenance-rich remote media references plus structured factual menu/offerings data without copying third-party binaries
Do not retain media or menu data
decisions.decision: Store provider-neutral remote media references and structured Business Offering facts with complete source/provenance. Do not copy third-party image binaries. Treat menu-item as the first generic offering kind, retain only data exposed by already-authorised public discovery sources, and materialise accepted records to the Business after confirmation without falsely marking unseen public media/menu facts as owner-confirmed.
decisions.rationale: The Product Owner explicitly instructed Atlas to store restaurant images when available and approved the sequence to add business-media capture followed by structured menu/menu-price ingestion. The selected approach preserves Atlas's provider-neutral core, data-minimisation policy and public-source safety boundary.

decisions.question: How should Atlas use a uniquely resolved Google Place to reduce repetitive onboarding while respecting owner authority and Google Places content restrictions?
options: Ask all operating questions manually and do not enrich
Fetch rich Place Details for every search candidate and persist the provider response

After one exact Place is selected, fetch one bounded Place Details response transiently, let the owner explicitly submit canonical operating answers, retain only the Place ID as Google provider content, then ask Goals first and suppress satisfied questions
decisions.decision: After Atlas uniquely resolves a Business to one Google Place, use at most one bounded Places API (New) Place Details request for the current owner interaction regardless of whether discovery began from a website, Bolt, Wolt or Google URL. Google rich response content remains transient and Atlas retains only the Place ID as Google provider content. Persist canonical operating context only through a separate explicit owner submit/confirm action; do not persist copied Google payloads, attribution payloads or hidden Google-derived facts. For sufficiently enriched Businesses, optional non-goal onboarding targets 0–3 questions, with five retained only as the degraded/missing-context ceiling. Goals remain owner-only and are presented before optional non-goal context.
decisions.rationale: The Product Owner approved the VS-26 design and implementation plan and instructed Atlas to proceed. The execution-time official Google policy review confirmed mandatory field masks, Place ID storage exemption, broader Places content storage/caching restrictions and EEA-specific permitted-use constraints, so the implementation adopts the stricter transient-content boundary.
